**Job Description

**_At Netcompany, we are looking for both newly graduated candidates with a relevant master’s degree – or equivalent experience – who want to work as IT Consultants at the intersection of technology, business, and people. Do you want to help develop some of Denmark’s most complex and business-critical IT solutions, where software development, project management, and close client collaboration are central parts of everyday work?

_**Responsibilities And Technologies

**As an IT Consultant, you help translate client needs into the right technical solution. We choose the technologies that best fit each project and client. As a result, you should enjoy working across a variety of technologies and domains, while continuously expanding your knowledge and expertise.

A large part of our projects is based on web technologies such as Angular or React, and Java or C# on either a Java or .NET platform. In addition, we work with a wide range of standard platforms including Microsoft, Salesforce, IBM, Oracle, Adobe, Snowflake, Guidewire, and others.

• Implementing features in user interfaces.

Our projects include some of Denmark’s most innovative and mission-critical IT initiatives across the public and private sectors, meaning you will help shape and improve everyday life for a large part of society.

• Are a recent graduate or have a couple of years of experience – most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Have a solid understanding of software development and are motivated to further develop your skills.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

As Chief Quantum Officer at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), you will bring the university’s quantum research communities together around shared priorities. You will build the relationships and partnerships needed to turn those priorities into joint initiatives and secure external funding for them.

DTU hosts internationally recognised research, innovation, and education activities across quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, quantum materials, and advanced quantum device fabrication. As discoveries in quantum science find new applications in industry and society, you will help shape DTU’s contribution in Denmark and internationally.

You will build on the foundations already in place, developing DTU’s quantum strategy further and leading its implementation. Working across technology, strategy and organisational development, you will turn strategic priorities into concrete initiatives and strengthen DTU’s ability to coordinate work across departments. You will build trust with researchers, industry partners, policymakers and funding organisations and bring them together around shared goals.

As a visible representative of DTU, you will strengthen collaboration with universities and other partners in Denmark and across the Nordic countries. You will also represent DTU’s interests in international policy discussions and help shape strategies that strengthen its position in the global quantum ecosystem.

Quantum DTU is DTU's central platform for quantum activities and serves as a catalyst for collaboration across disciplines, departments, and external partners. It is anchored in the Office of Scientific Advice, Defence and Resilience, which is a part of the Department for Research, Advice and Innovation. You will work closely with DTU’s departments and central administration, drawing on their expertise in research, strategy, partnerships and organisational support.

Primary areas of responsibility

Strategic leadership and organisational development

• Lead the implementation and continued development of DTU's quantum strategy, translating strategic ambitions into concrete initiatives, partnerships, and measurable outcomes.
• Further develop Quantum DTU as DTU's coordinating platform for strategic quantum initiatives across research, innovation, education, and external partnerships.
• Advise DTU leadership on strategic opportunities, investments, and developments within the quantum field. 
• Develop Quantum DTU's organisational capabilities, structures, and networks in close collaboration with DTU's departments and relevant central administrative functions.
• Support the Chair and Steering Committee of Quantum DTU in strategic planning, preparation of decisions, and follow-up on agreed priorities and initiatives.
Partnerships and stakeholder engagement

• Represent DTU in national and international quantum initiatives, networks, and partnerships. 
• Establish and maintain strategic relationships with public authorities, funding agencies, industry partners, investors, and international organisations. 
• Strengthen DTU's position within the Danish, European, and international quantum 
research, innovation, and policy agendas through partnerships and engagement.

Research, innovation, and ecosystem development

• Drive collaboration across DTU's quantum-related research, education, and innovation activities.
• Facilitate internal coordination, knowledge sharing, and collaboration across DTU's quantum research environments and departments.
• Contribute to strategic initiatives, major funding opportunities, and resource planning in collaboration with relevant administrative functions.
• Promote the translation of quantum research into societal, industrial, and commercial impact. 
• Facilitate engagement with key stakeholders through workshops, strategic initiatives, and high-level visits and delegations.
Your background
You bring substantial knowledge of and experience in quantum science or technology. You can discuss scientific and technological developments with researchers, earn their trust and use your expertise to help set a direction for DTU’s quantum activities.

Ideal profile and qualifications:

• You have experience in quantum science or technology or a solid understanding of the scientific and technological developments shaping the field.
• You have significant insight into the quantum field and can engage effectively with leading researchers and build trust across DTU’s quantum research community.
• You combine technical insight with strategic and political awareness, and you understand how academia, industry and public-sector stakeholders work together to drive technological development.
• You have demonstrated experience in research leadership, project or programme management, and in bringing people from different disciplines together to work towards shared objectives.
• You have experience building organisations, programmes, partnerships or ecosystems in collaboration with academic and administrative stakeholders.
• You excel at building relationships and have strong communication, facilitation and stakeholder management skills.
• You can communicate complex technological topics to diverse audiences.
• You hold a relevant advanced degree in science, engineering, technology, innovation, public policy or a related field. 
What we offer

• A unique opportunity to shape DTU's future role within quantum technologies.
• A highly visible strategic role with broad internal and external engagement.
• The opportunity to build and develop Quantum DTU as a strategic platform.
• An ambitious, international, and collaborative working environment. 
Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Senior Officer or Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The position is permanent and full-time (37 hours per week). Starting date as soon as possible (according to mutual agreement). 

The workplace is DTU Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact

Please submit your online application no later than 6 December 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. Candidates should expect two rounds of interviews as part of the recruitment process.

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Office, Kasper Dam Schultz, +45 61 33 51 20 kadam@dtu.dk. Read more about DTU at www.dtu.dk. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Electronic-Photonic Integration: Merging Photonic and CMOS Chips for Scalable Information Processing - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
The rapid growth of artificial intelligence has made data movement a key bottleneck in computing hardware. Integrated photonics is therefore increasingly used to interconnect electronic processors at a far lower energy per bit than electrical links. Scaling up photonic circuits themselves also requires integrated electronics for large-scale control and stabilization of many optical components in applications, such as biomedical imaging and control of atom-based quantum computers. We offer a PhD scholarship at DTU Electro, where you will develop the 3D integration of photonic and CMOS chips forming the foundation for future technologies.

Our photonic circuits are made in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), which is transparent from the visible to the mid-infrared. Its electro-optic effect allows fast modulation of light without adding optical loss. Our team has recently shown that photonic crystal cavities in TFLN can serve as ultracompact modulators [1] with electrically controllable coupling to waveguides [2], and they can route light between many ports [3]. Small cavities need little energy to drive, but their resonances drift with temperature and fabrication variations. Scaling up circuits therefore requires alignment and stabilization of all resonators via local electronic feedback in addition to high-speed modulation. We work closely with our collaborators at Harvard University, whose research has shaped the TFLN field [4]. 

In the project EPIC, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark, you will contribute to the design, fabrication, and characterization of devices that join TFLN photonic circuits to custom CMOS chips from our microelectronics team by flip-chip bonding. The aim is to keep many resonator-based modulators, driven at gigahertz speeds, stable at visible and near-infrared wavelengths across a chip. This calls for careful co-design of the photonics with integrated photodetectors, feedback circuits, and drive electronics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will help drive the experimental work in EPIC from co-design to demonstration. You will work closely with Professor Per Lynggaard's CMOS design team, other PhD students, postdocs, and senior researchers at DTU, and our collaborators at Harvard University. Depending on your interests, you will have the opportunity to:

• Co-design photonic cavities, couplers, and electronic interfaces using optical, thermal, and circuit simulations.
• Fabricate photonic circuits in DTU Nanolab’s state-of-the-art cleanroom.
• Develop flip-chip bonding of photonic and CMOS chips.
• Explore feedback schemes that stabilize many cavities across a chip.
• Characterize assembled devices using high-speed electro-optic measurements.
• Present your results at international conferences and in leading journals.
You enjoy hands-on laboratory work and learning across disciplines, and you take ownership of the progress and quality of your work.

Required qualifications:

• A strong background in photonics, optics, or electronics.
• Experimental experience in photonics, optics, or electronics, e.g., from your master’s project.
• Programming experience in Python.
Desired qualifications:

• Nanofabrication or integrated photonics.
• Analog circuit design or high-speed electronics.
• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.description:
Are you driven by detecting, investigating and stopping security threats, and do you want to help strengthen how a global company protects its business every day?

“Our Security Operations team protects Arla’s systems and data around the clock. In this role, you will take ownership of key parts of our detection and response capabilities, work closely with our security service providers to continuously improve them, and share your expertise with colleagues across IT,” says Poul Henrik Tang Jensen, Senior Manager, Head of IT Product.

How you will make an impact

You will join IT Security Operations within IT Foundation, where you will take ownership of assigned Security Operations capabilities across endpoint, identity, network, application and cloud environments. Our technology landscape includes Microsoft and Palo Alto security technologies across SIEM, XDR, endpoint and identity.

You will work closely with our managed security service providers, who perform much of the day-to-day security monitoring, investigation and technical execution. Your role is to ensure these services deliver the detection, response and protection capabilities Arla needs.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Taking ownership of assigned Security Operations capabilities and ensuring they remain effective, relevant and aligned with Arla’s risks and business needs.

• 
Overseeing security monitoring and investigations performed by our managed security service providers, challenging findings and providing technical direction on complex cases and incidents.

• 
Coordinating incident response across service providers and internal teams, including containment, eradication, recovery, escalation and follow-up.

• 
Driving improvements to detection rules, correlation logic, automation workflows and incident-response playbooks, working with our service providers on implementation.

• 
Assessing vulnerabilities and security-control weaknesses

• 
Managing the technical quality and performance of our security service providers, setting priorities and ensuring agreed improvements are implemented.

• 
Providing practical, risk-based security advice and assessments to projects and product teams.

• 
Leading Security Operations improvement initiatives and sharing security expertise across IT.

What will make you successful

You take ownership and follow issues through to a clear conclusion. When a security incident unfolds, you remain calm, analytical and decisive. You are comfortable working independently, while recognising when collaboration or escalation is needed. The ideal candidate brings:

• A relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree in IT, cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• Typically 5+ years of relevant cybersecurity experience, including substantial experience within Security Operations, security monitoring, investigation and incident response.

• Experience taking ownership of complex security investigations, incidents or operational security improvements, including coordinating technical activities across internal teams and external security providers.

• Solid technical knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, EDR, network and identity-security monitoring, and vulnerability management.

• Practical understanding of attacker techniques and security frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST and ISO 27001.

• Good understanding of security logging, telemetry, evidence collection and forensic-analysis principles.

• Good understanding of security queries, scripting and automation, enabling you to assess technical solutions, challenge implementation choices and drive improvements with security service providers.

• Experience working with and providing technical direction to managed security service providers, while collaborating effectively with internal technology and product teams.

• A relevant professional security certification, or equivalent demonstrable expertise.

• Experience with technologies such as Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, KQL, Palo Alto or similar enterprise security platforms would be an advantage.

What do we offer?

This position is based in either Aarhus, Denmark or Gdansk, Poland. You will be part of an on-call rotation, approximately every seventh week, to provide support in case of critical issues.

You will join a skilled and collaborative IT Security Operations team with a central role in protecting a global market leader. You will have real ownership of our Security Operations capabilities and the opportunity to lead technical workstreams and improvement initiatives.

Would you like to join us?

If you want to help keep Arla secure and make our Security Operations capabilities even stronger, we would love to hear from you. Please apply as soon as possible, as we review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the recruitment once the right candidate has been found.

For more information, please contact Poul Henrik Tang Jensen, Senior Manager, Head of IT Product Security Operations, at pohtj@arlafoods.com.

jobs.description:
Professor of Psychotherapy
 (Part-Time or Clinical Appointment, Fixed-Term for 5 Years)

  Department of Clinical Medicine
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
  University of Copenhagen

  The University of Copenhagen invites applications for a professorship in Psychotherapy. Depending on the qualifications and current position of the successful applicant, the appointment will be made either as a part-time professor combined with a senior researcher position, or as a clinical professor combined with a consultancy at one of the hospitals listed below.

  • Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg, the Mental Health Centre Copenhagen

  • Copenhagen University Hospital – Herlev and Gentofte, Center Stolpegaard

  It is a requirement for appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the professorship and the consultancy/position as senior researcher. In order to be considered for the position, the applicant must send two applications: one to the Faculty (the professorship) and one to the hospital (the consultancy/senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the consultancy/position as senior researcher. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at one of the hospitals. The advertisements for the consultancies/senior researcher positions are available at:

   	
• Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg: https://www.sundhedsjobs.dk 	
• Copenhagen University Hospital – Herlev and Gentofte: https://www.sundhedsjobs.dk   Both the professorship and the consultancy/position as senior researcher will be financed by the relevant hospital.

  Find information about the department.

  Job description
 In the consideration of applications for the professorship, the main emphasis will be on the applicant's ability to document a high level of original scientific work at an international level within the area of psychiatry or psychology.

  The professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination. The realization of psychotherapeutic treatment of patients with psychiatric disorders, including new technologies, implies great potential. The professorship aims to ensure the scientific development of psychotherapeutic treatment of patients with psychiatric disorders, including outcome - and process studies, and new technologies as a supplement to psychotherapeutic practice, and to ensure implementation in clinical practice.   	
• Research-based teaching, including associated examination. The professor shall conduct research-based teaching in psychotherapy within different psychiatric disorders, including new technologies. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers. The professor shall overall plan and develop research initiatives within psychotherapy and aid in implementing results into clinical practice. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for a professorship, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, Teaching, Innovation & Societal impact, Organizational contribution, and Leadership. Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to:

   	
• Document a high degree of original academic production at an international level, including considerable contributions to the development of the academic discipline 	
• Manage research and other management functions, e.g. engage in the university’s external academic activities, as well as knowledge and technology transfer 	
• Provide research-based teaching   The professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. The position is a fixed-term positions limited to a period of five years. Extension is possible.

  The employers in the combined position may, where necessary, exchange information regarding matters that are of significant relevance to the employment relationship.

  Terms of employment especially for the professor (part time)
 For the position as professor the average weekly working hours are approximately 11 hours per week. Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  This form of employment shall remain in effect until, pursuant to the applicable Job structure for Aacademic Staff, the appointment of non-medical professionals as Clinical Professors becomes possible and an agreement on salary and employment terms for such positions has been concluded with the relevant professional organisations. Upon fulfilment of these conditions, the employment shall be converted to an appointment as Clinical Professor, in accordance with the description set out below.

  Terms of employment especially for the clinical professor
 For the clinical professorship the appointee will receive a pensionable annual honorarium of 219.882,33 DKK (1 August 2026 level)

  Questions
 For further information please contact Head of Department Nicolai W. Albrechtsen, nicolai.albrechtsen@regionh.dk.

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates) 	
• Uploads of maximum 10 publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Self-declaration form (Template under ‘Nyttige links’ - Upload the completed and mandatory form as “Other relevant material”) 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines / Template for inspiration under Nyttige links) 	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• A complete list of publications   Application procedure 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee. When the assessment committee has completed the assessment, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Wednesday, 9 December 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 19 April 2027.

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

**Job Description

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

jobs.description:
Product Management at Dalux – Turning Information into Attention

Construction projects generate an enormous amount of information. Files change. Tasks are assigned. Deadlines approach. Comments are added. Reviews require action. Issues are reported. People are mentioned. Workflows progress. But more information does not necessarily make people better informed.

Dalux is looking for a Product Manager to take dedicated ownership of Notifications and help us answer a deceptively difficult product question:

How do we make sure users know what requires their attention – without overwhelming them with information?

Notifications exist throughout our products today, across email, mobile, and in-product experiences. As Dalux has grown, so has their complexity. We believe this area deserves dedicated product ownership and a coherent strategy across our products.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Notification Strategy: Define a coherent product direction for how Dalux communicates important events and required actions to users.

• Product Discovery: Understand when users need to be informed, when they need to take action, and when a notification simply creates unnecessary noise.

• Customer Insights: Research how different users manage information and attention across complex projects and busy working days.

• Cross-product Ownership: Map and improve notification experiences across Dalux products rather than optimizing individual notifications in isolation.

• Channels & Preferences: Develop experiences spanning in-app notifications, email, mobile push, notification preferences, subscriptions, following, mentions, reminders, and digests.

• Relevance & Prioritization: Explore grouping, prioritization, timing, and deduplication to ensure important information stands out.

• Actionability: Make notifications useful by ensuring users understand why they received them, what has changed, and what action they should take.

• Product Analytics: Use quantitative and qualitative insights to understand which notifications create value and which create noise.

• Shared Capabilities: Work with Development and other Product Managers to create common notification principles and platform capabilities that can be reused across Dalux.

About You

You probably don't currently have "Notifications Product Manager" as your job title – and that's perfectly fine.

We're looking for an experienced Product Manager who finds the underlying problem interesting and has the product and systems thinking required to solve it.

We believe you:

• Have strong Product Management experience, preferably from B2B SaaS, collaboration, productivity, workflow, communication, or similar software.

• Have excellent product discovery and UX instincts.

• Think systematically and can turn many individual use cases into coherent product concepts.

• Understand the tension between keeping users informed and creating notification fatigue.

• Are comfortable owning a horizontal capability spanning multiple products and development teams.

• Can combine user research with product analytics to understand behavior.

• Care about interaction details and understand how seemingly small product decisions can have a large cumulative impact on user experience.

• Can simplify complex systems involving events, recipients, relevance, timing, preferences, and communication channels.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Construction Technology Experience Is Welcome But Not Required .

Experience from collaboration, communication, workflow, or productivity software would be particularly relevant.

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives
